library_preparation_preflight.summary: Avro 1.12.2 added a ClassSecurityValidator allow-list gate on reflect/specific-data (de)serialization; test-declared record classes now throw SecurityException unless trusted via org.apache.avro.SERIALIZABLE_CLASSES/SERIALIZABLE_PACKAGES system properties.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Generated tests that exercise reflect-based or specific-data (de)serialization of test-declared record classes (e.g. via ReflectDatumWriter/ReflectDatumReader, SpecificData.getClass/getNewRecordSupplier, or any encodeRecord/decodeRecord helper that touches classes under the generated package) will hit org.apache.avro.util.ClassSecurityValidator's default deny-list starting with avro 1.12.2. Trust the generated test package by adding a JVM system property, e.g. in the test task's jvmArgs: -Dorg.apache.avro.SERIALIZABLE_PACKAGES=org_apache_avro.avro (match whatever package the generated test classes actually live under). This must be set as a JVM-level -D flag (or equivalent Gradle jvmArgs), not via System.setProperty() inside test code, because ClassSecurityValidator.SystemPropertiesPredicate reads the property once in a static initializer at class-load time, so setting it later in a test method or @BeforeAll has no effect. Alternatively, tests may call the org.apache.avro.util.ClassSecurityValidator API (e.g. ClassSecurityValidator.setGlobal(...)) directly before any schema-related class loading occurs, but the jvmArgs system-property approach mirrors the existing pattern already used in this project's build.gradle (-Djdk.invoke.LambdaMetafactory.dumpProxyClassFiles=true) and is simpler to keep correct.
risks: If the generated test package differs from org_apache_avro.avro, the SERIALIZABLE_PACKAGES value must be updated to match, or affected tests will still fail with SecurityException.

Setting the property programmatically after JVM/class-loader startup (e.g. via System.setProperty in a test method) will silently not take effect since the predicate is cached at class-load time — must be a JVM start-up level -D flag.
